item.title: Houston's O'Shaquie Foster drops Emanuel Navarrete twice, takes his belts at 130 pounds
item.description: O'Shaquie Foster knocks down Emanuel Navarrete. Emanuel Navarrete and Texas native O'Shaquie Foster meet for the IBF, WBC and WBO world super featherweight titles on Saturday, Oct. 24,2026 at Frost Bank Center (Ronald Cortes) Emmanuel Navarrete entered the ring Saturday night as the boxer with the reputation of being a power puncher who finishes fights. However, it was O'Shaquie Foster, who grew up in Orange and lives and trains in Houston , standing over a thoroughly beaten Navarrete after a pair of 12th round knockdowns at San Antonio's Frost Bank Center on his way to a unanimous 118-108, 118-108, 115-111 decision to hold on to his World Boxing Council junior lightweight title, while taking Navarrete's World Boxing Organization and International Boxing Federation belts. "I told y'all before, I'm the better inside fighter and the better outside fighter and I feel like I proved that tonight," Foster said in the ring immediately after the win. "Hats off to him, but I knew I was levels above him and I just wanted to prove it." The 31-year-old Navarrete (40-3-1, 33 KOs) came out aggressively and the two fighters battled pretty evenly for the first four rounds, but Foster (26-3, 12 KOs) began to take control in the fifth round with effective counter punching and a sharpshooting right hand. "In this sport, it's about styles," Navarrete said. "His style was better than mine tonight." The hard-hitting Navarrete landed some power shots throughout the fight, including a right uppercut to the chin in the final 10 seconds of the 11th round that seemed to hurt Foster, but the champion held firm. "Hell yeah, he can punch, but I've got a chin," Foster admitted. "I'm strong." Although trying to determine how judges saw a fight always can be risky, it seemed pretty clear that Foster was ahead on the scorecards entering the 12th, but he was the one who chose to come out aggressively for the final round. Navarrete, who entered the night having tasted the canvas just once in his career, went down twice in the 12th. "My coaches just told me, 'Go out and put him on his ass' and that's what I did," Foster said. The first knockdown came with an overhand right, then he got him again with a right hook to the chin. "I felt like was breaking him down throughout the fight and I just timed him good in that last round," Foster said. With Foster holding three belts at 130 pounds now, he needs just to grab the World Boxing Association strap to become the first junior lightweight to unify the division since it expanded to four belts. Anthony Cacace defends his WBA belt against Nick Ball in December. "I'm trying to go undisputed for sure, so the winner out of Cacace and Ball, come see me," Foster said. Foster has long talked about getting a shot at unbeaten Shakur Stevenson, who jumped in the ring after Foster beat Raymond Ford at University of Houston's Fertitta Center and seemed to agree to fight his former training partner turned rival. However, Stevenson has jumped up to 140

item.title: Man United consider Bundesliga solution after major investment in attack and midfield
item.description: Man United consider Bundesliga solution after major investment in attack and midfield Manchester United are reportedly prioritising a move for RB Leipzig defender David Raum as Michael Carrick looks to strengthen his defensive options ahead of the January transfer window. According to a report from CaughtOffside , the Germany international has become a top target for the Red Devils, who are preparing to address backline weaknesses after investing heavily elsewhere in the squad. David Raum could be an ideal defensive addition The 28-year-old has established himself as a reliable Bundesliga performer, combining defensive aggression with the ability to contribute effectively in attack. Manchester United are keen to improve their left-back options, and Raum could offer an experienced solution to their ongoing concerns in that position. His ability to deliver dangerous crosses, support attacking transitions and contribute defensively would make him an attractive addition to Carrick’s squad. United have explored several alternatives, including Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite. However, Raum is believed to be one of the more attainable options available to the Premier League giants. His contract situation could also work in United’s favour. The defender’s current agreement with Leipzig expires in the summer of 2027, which could encourage the German club to sell in January rather than risk losing him for a reduced fee later. Manchester United could secure a bargain deal for Raum Despite his importance to Leipzig, Raum could represent a financially sensible option for United compared with younger defenders commanding substantial transfer fees. The Germany international is reportedly open to testing himself in the Premier League, which could strengthen the Red Devils’ position if negotiations progress. Manchester United have already invested heavily in their attack and midfield, and defensive reinforcements are now becoming a priority. Raum’s experience and versatility could help address those concerns without requiring the club to commit an excessive fee. However, Leipzig must first decide whether they are prepared to sanction his departure midway through the campaign. With January approaching, United could accelerate their pursuit if an agreement emerges. Raum remains a promising option as Carrick looks to build a more balanced and dependable defensive unit. item.title: Stoever shuts out Steelers as Devils claim cup win
item.description: Man of the match Christian Stoever saved 31 shots for his second shutout of the season [James Assinder] Cardiff Devils took another step towards the Challenge Cup knockout stages with a tense home win against Group A leaders Sheffield Steelers. Kristoff Kontos scored the games only goal after 43 seconds of the first period, with Devils' netminder Christian Stoever making a string of outstanding saves to protect the home side's lead. The visitors also struck the pipework twice, while Cardiff's Riley Brandt and Nick Welsh went close. Despite the 1-0 final scoreline, Devils' head coach Paul Thompson described the game as a "classic win". "An absolute battle for 60 minutes, and Sheffield are a very, very good team," he said. "They probably had more offensive zone time against us than any team has had this year, but when they did get inside I thought [Stoever] was outstanding. "Sometimes you've just got to roll your sleeves up and battle, and that's what we did." With two games remaining for Cardiff they lie in third place on eight points, two behind Sheffield and Nottingham Panthers who both only have one more game to play in the group stage. Devils travel to Nottingham on Sunday, 25 October (16:00 GMT) before their final game at Manchester Storm on Sunday, 1 November. Guildford Flames, in fourth, also have 10 points with a final game at Coventry Blaze this weekend. Their hosts - and Storm - are not completely out of the running for third spot having played fewer games. The top two sides in Group A automatically qualify for the semi-final, with the third-placed team facing an elimination tie against the runners-up in the smaller group B. GB men and women to make history in Glasgow

item.title: Texas coach Steve Sarkisian calls out ticket sellers: 'They missed a hell of a game.'
item.description: AUSTIN, TX – Steve Sarkisian expressed gratitude for the Texas faithful who filled the stadium to the gills for the team’s 34-27 takedown of No. 7 Mississippi, but he also called out some apparent ticket sellers. “It was a nice night in DKR,” the Texas coach said. “For our fans, I can’t thank them enough. What an amazing atmosphere and energy DKR was again. For those fans that sold their tickets, they missed a hell of a game tonight.” If some fans sold their tickets, there was clearly a vibrant resale market, because the crowd of 104,306 exceeded the stadium’s official capacity and ranked as the fourth-largest crowd in the stadium’s history. The crowd got treated to a virtuoso performance from Texas in the first half, a furious rally from Ole Miss in the third quarter, and a game-winning touchdown run from Arch Manning on a bootleg, when he could’ve been confused for Uncle Peyton. “We’ve had that play in all season,” Manning said of his winning scoring run. He duped the Rebels with the play-fake and scored without a defender in sight. “It felt good, No one was around.” Texas overcame three turnovers and 121 penalty yards and earned another signature victory. This pelt goes alongside the September victory against Ohio State and polishes the Texas resume after it endured back-to-back SEC losses. Raleek Brown rushed for 157 yards for Texas, and the Longhorns defense made it tough on Ole Miss star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who threw three interceptions, including one on the game's final play. “I thought we played with Texas fight," Sarkisian said. "I thought we played with a lot of pride.” A full-house crowd saw Texas save its season. Blake Toppmeyer is the USA TODAY Network's senior national college football columnist. Listen to his podcast, " College Football Unfiltered ." Email him at BToppmeyer@gannett.com and follow him on X @btoppmeyer . item.title: Behind the scenes of a 1st NHL goal
item.description: Fans cheer for the sixth goal of the game for the Utah Mammoth as they and the Chicago Blackhawks play an NHL game at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News Both the Tampa Bay Lightning and the Utah Mammoth got to clear the bench to celebrate goals at the Delta Center Saturday night. When the game ended, though, the Mammoth were the only happy team. It was an evening to remember. Lightning superstar and reigning MVP Nikita Kucherov scored his 1,138th point to take sole possession of the franchise lead in points. That happened in the first period, so the Bolts got their bench clearing out of the way early. Bolts clear the bench to celebrate pic.twitter.com/VjFEKhFvjj — Brogan Houston (@houston_brogan) October 25, 2026 The Mammoth surmounted a 4-2 deficit to force overtime, thanks in part to Dmitri Simashev’s first NHL goal, which tied the game. Utah’s bench clearing came at the hands of Simashev a little while later, when he scored the second goal of his career — and the overtime winner. Final score: 5-4 Mammoth. “It’s fun to see um a young player like Sima come in, play the way he has all year but then get rewarded tonight with a big one,” said Utah forward Anders Lee, who also scored in the game. “Big night that I think he’ll remember for a long time.” Coincidentally, Simashev’s first two KHL goals came in similar fashion to these first two in the NHL. As was the case for him in the NHL, he went his entire first season without scoring a goal. His first one eventually came in the third period of a game, and his second came in overtime (albeit a few games later). If the past can be taken as any indication of future events, Simashev might be due for another goal soon. In the KHL, he scored his third two games after his second. Mammoth head coach André Tourigny mentioned that the game is finally starting to “slow down” for the big Russian defenseman. When coaches use that term, they mean the player feels less pressure and more confidence to make the right play. It’s a good thing. It was somewhat unexpected to see No. 26 on the ice in overtime in the first place. He has been defensively sound since he got to the NHL, but OT requires an offensive edge and Simashev hadn’t owned an NHL first-goal puck for more than an hour by the time he jumped over the boards. That’s without mentioning the fact that Utah has plenty of two-way defensemen who could have taken the assignment. Tourigny said it was defensive coach Adam Foote’s call. “Footer came to me after the the third period. You can say (we) overused some guys, and he felt Sima had legs and he was fresh, or more fresh than other guys, so he asked me, and I trust Footer’s feeling and his feel for the game, so went with that,” Tourigny said. “It was pretty good. That was a pretty good call.” Simashev thought the same thing. “I didn’t expect I’m going in overtime, to be honest. Like, thanks Footer to trust in me, and, I mean, I was just so happy when

item.title: Dodgers announcer calls for MLB to make major change after Rays' Yandy Diaz check swing controversy
item.description: Dodgers announcer calls for MLB to make major change after Rays' Yandy Diaz check swing controversy originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Entering Monday night, the Tampa Bay Rays were down one game after losing to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1. The Rays have refused to give up all season, and nothing less is expected of them now. Tampa Bay couldn’t have written a better start to the game. In the top of the first inning, Liam Hicks hit the first home run of the World Series to put the Rays up 4-0. “The World Series opener was all about small ball, featuring 12 singles, three stolen bases and no home runs – the first Fall Classic Game 1 without a homer since 2000. Liam Hicks muscled up and changed that narrative early, belting a two-run homer in the first inning of World Series Game 2 on Saturday evening at American Family Field that helped power the Rays’ early 4-0 lead,” MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch wrote. Those were the only runs the Rays would score on the night. The Brewers went on to win the game. “The Brewers pulled off a stunning 5-4 victory over the Rays at American Family Field, taking a 2-0 lead in their bid for the first World Series championship in franchise history. Really, at this point, there may be no stopping them. The Brewers were down 4-0 just five batters into the game, teasing the Rays that they were going to win, and then methodically came back to rip their hearts out,” USA Today’s Bob Nightengale wrote. However, the final play of the game was as controversial as it gets. Yandy Díaz checked his swing, but when the umpire was asked to appeal the call, he ruled that Díaz had swung, ending the game. After seeing the replay, World Series and Los Angeles Dodgers announcer Joe Davis called on MLB to implement a replay system for check swings, similar to the one used for balls and strikes. “We got ABS for the first time this year, getting the balls and strikes right; we need to get a system that can get [check-swings] right,” Davis said. "We got ABS for the first time this year, getting the balls and strikes right; we need to get a system that can get [check-swings] right." - Joe Davis https://t.co/PVQ1X9S4qf — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 25, 2026 There is no doubt that it is a heartbreaking way to lose in such a big moment. If it wasn’t a swing, the call would have kept the game alive with a walk. Díaz was frustrated, as he felt he hadn’t swung. Davis has a valid reason to call for change, as a replay system could have helped resolve the controversy surrounding the final play. Following this incident and Davis’ call for a solution, MLB could consider implementing a check-swing review system for next season. item.title: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane wins the Spanish version of the Ballon d’Or
item.description: Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images | Getty Images Ahead of the 2026 Ballon d’Or awarding ceremony, Bayern Munich star Harry Kane is the favorite to win the award. Interestingly, the Englishman picked up the Spanish equivalent of the Ballon d’Or by winning the “100 Marca” award presented by Spanish news outlet Marca (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ): 🏆 Harry Kane has won the ‘100 Marca’ award by @marca for the best player of the 25-26 season. Kane was voted by an international jury of 226 members, including journalists from MARCA, journalists from many other media outlets in Spain and around the world, former footballers, and coaches. Top 10: 1- Kane (3,962 points) 2- Yamal (3,937) 3- Mbappé (3,440) 4- Rodri 5- Kvaratskhelia 6- Messi 7- Fabián Ruiz 8- Olise 9- Dembélé 10- Cubarsí Kane succeeds previous winners Karim Benzema (21-22), Erling Haaland (22-23), Vinicius Jr (23-24) and Lamine Yamal (24-25). Here’s a video of Kane reacting to winning 100 Marca: Harry Kane's message after winning the '100 Marca' award for the best player of 2025/26 🏆 pic.twitter.com/glPOnP30zm — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) October 23, 2026 This award is like the Ballon d’Or in many ways: the voting and point-scoring systems, the evaluation period (the full 2025/26 season), and, to an extent, the number of nominees. As the name suggests, Kane emerged as the best player out of 100 players on Marca’s shortlist, compared to the Ballon d’Or, which lists 30 players. Interestingly, Kane finishing in first place meant he beat fellow Ballon d’Or contenders Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé, who finished second and third behind the Englishman in a poll where a good chunk of the panel is made up of journalists across Spain. Could we see the same rankings on Monday? Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Travis Kelce gets major injury update as NFL makes controversial Daiyan Henley decision
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Travis Kelce has received a positive injury update ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs’ meeting with the Seattle Seahawks, despite the NFL deciding against punishing Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for the tackle that injured him. Kelce suffered an ankle injury during the Chiefs’ victory over the Chargers after a tackle that sparked questions about whether Henley had committed a hip-drop tackle. The NFL has since issued its disciplinary decisions for the relevant round of games, but Henley escaped a fine while another Chargers player was punished. Travis Kelce cleared to face Seattle Seahawks as Daiyan Henley avoids NFL punishment The Chiefs listed Kelce as a limited participant throughout the week because of his ankle problem. However, he entered the weekend without an injury designation, indicating he is available for the Seahawks matchup. Kelce initially went down in the opening quarter against the Chargers after what appeared to be a hip-drop tackle. Despite the injury, he returned to the game after the Chiefs’ medical staff taped his ankle. The veteran tight end finished with four catches for 53 yards as Kansas City secured a 22-6 victory. However, the NFL’s Office of Gameday Accountability did not include Henley among the players fined for on-field misconduct. The decision could frustrate Chiefs supporters who believed the tackle warranted disciplinary action. PJ Green of the Kansas City Star had described the incident on X, writing : “Daiyan Henley’s tackle on Travis Kelce was a sliding hip drop where his shoulder dinged Kelce’s ankle.” While Henley avoided punishment, Chargers rookie offensive guard Alex Harkey was fined $5,277 for a late hit against Kansas City early in the fourth quarter. Kelce’s availability is welcome news for the Chiefs as they look to maintain their unbeaten start to the season. A victory over the defending champion Seahawks would take Kansas City to 6-0 and keep them at the top of the AFC standings. With Patrick Mahomes and Kelce available, the Chiefs have received a timely boost ahead of a challenging road test. The focus now shifts to whether they can extend their winning run against Seattle. item.title: Texas football fans react to Longhorns' win over Ole Miss: 'A win when we needed it most'
item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning runs into the end zone untouched for a fourth quarter touchdown against Mississippi at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) After losing two straight games, the Texas Longhorns needed to pull off the upset over visiting Ole Miss to keep College Football Playoffs alive. And No. 19 Texas did just that with a 34-27 win over the No. 7 Rebels that came down to the wire. A pair of Longhorns (5-2, 2-2 SEC) failed to recover an onside kick and Ole Miss (5-2, 3-2) couldn't find the end zone. The Longhorns relied on its rushing attack and quarterback Arch Manning scored his first rushing touchdowns of the season while running back Raleek Brown finished the night with 157 yards. After being the subject of conversation over the last few weeks, Texas' special teams blocked a go-ahead field goal in the fourth quarter. Here is how social media reacted to Texas' win: LONGHORNS WIN!!! I DON'T THINK I'VE TAKEN A REAL BREATH IN ABOUT 5 MINUTES! THEY INTERCEPTED THE DAMN BALL IN THE ENDZONE FOR THE WIN!!! #HookEm https://t.co/cVHW8NqZHT - Ally (@OhMyItsAlly) October 25, 2026 What a win when we needed it the most!! #HookEm - VARi 🦅 (@VariBlessed) October 25, 2026 I swear, when I die, my death certificate is going to say, 'Cause of death: Texas Athletics.' Ha. #HookEm 😂😂 Onward. - Nick Ⓜ️ (@TheN1ckM) October 25, 2026 Will be watching Tangled next Saturday and every Saturday going forward. 🫡🤘 #Hookem - Michelle (@michellelynnn94) October 25, 2026 Texas' run game got it done Texas coach Steve Sarkisian realizing Arch Manning cant throw an interception to Ole Miss if you keep handing the ball off https://t.co/KGC5XrSh6I - Mike (@Mike4yag) October 25, 2026 #Hookem https://t.co/ClfuVbYUCX - Leah Vann (@LVann_Sports) October 25, 2026 Raleek Brown, I'm sorry I ever doubted you. Appreciate you bandaid 🩹 #HookEm - Bryson Wade (@BrysonWade3) October 25, 2026 Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) runs past Mississippi Rebels safety Sharif Denson (7) for a touchdown in the first quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. item.title: “Very important day”: Fabrizio Romano details United players’ true feelings on Carrick ahead of Bournemouth clash
item.description: “Very important day”: Fabrizio Romano details United players’ true feelings on Carrick ahead of Bournemouth clash Manchester United suffered one of their most embarrassing European outings in Italy on Wednesday, enduring a 4-1 defeat to Champions League debutants Como. That result extended United’s winless run to seven games, and yet, it was not enough for INEOS to pull the trigger on their second failed appointment after Ruben Amorim. However, Bruno Fernandes’ post-match interview suggested the cracks are widening at Carrington and Carrick is on borrowed time. What Manchester United players think of Michael Carrick Now, Fabrizio Romano has shed some light on the atmosphere behind the scenes at United ahead of a potentially season-defining clash against Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Speaking on his YouTube channel, the Italian journalist underlined, “It’s Sunday and it’s an important day for Manchester United, a very important day for Manchester United.” It is understood United decided to give Michael Carrick more time after the Como game in order to “evaluate the situation from now to the international break. That’s why Carrick went to the media on Friday.” Carrick insisted he completely trusts the team, but Romano claims “there are some issues with the players.” The United legend is thought to be “considered by everyone at Manchester United, players, board, directors, everyone, as a fantastic person. So he has respect from everyone. It’s not about the personal relationship. Sometimes it’s about tactics, sometimes it’s about decisions. There are some players that were not happy. That’s very clear after the Como game.” Talks over potentially replacing Carrick started Romano added that United have already held internal discussions to understand “what could be the direction for a new manager if they decide to part ways with Michael Carrick.” There may be some tension at board level at the club as well, with different figures favouring different names to potentially replace Carrick. “The German part” of the United hierarchy, presumably Christopher Vivell, admire Julian Nagelsmann and Fabian Hürzeler, while some prefer Eddie Howe. Director of football, Jason Wilcox, in particular, wants someone with Premier League experience to take over the helm. Featured image George Wood via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Roberto De Zerbi hails Mateus Fernandes' elite mentality as Tottenham break Stamford Bridge curse
item.description: Chelsea FC v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi was full of praise for his squad’s psychological shift following a dominant display in west London. The Italian tactician highlighted the performance of Mateus Fernandes, who remained composed throughout a high-tension London derby that saw tempers boil over in the second half. Fernandes shines in rare Bridge triumph Tottenham produced a tactical masterclass to secure a rare 2-0 victory against Chelsea , marking only their second Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 36 years. They took full advantage of a disciplined performance and a moment of madness from Cole Palmer to silence the home crowd. De Zerbi commended his squad's fighting spirit on the pitch, singling out Fernandes for delivering 90 minutes of exceptional quality. "I love watching my players fighting on the pitch. Fernandes played 90 minutes with a big quality. I want to see him with personality, enjoying with the ball, can make a mistake, it doesn’t matter. I want to see this personality from my team. We are a big club. In the last period the results have been not so good, but we are a top club. We must show personality. We must show mentality," De Zerbi said. Youthful energy fuels Tottenham resurgence With a one-man advantage, Tottenham doubled their lead through a stunning solo effort from Mathys Tel, who cut inside from the left wing to fire past Penders. The goal capped an impressive individual performance and highlighted the growing influence of the club’s younger stars. De Zerbi noted that the development of these prospects is central to his long-term vision for the team. "Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. Mateus Fernandes maybe was one of the best players on the pitch, like Mathys Tel. Archie Gray is younger, but he’s older as a mentality. I’m very, very happy. We want to improve, improve, improve, to be better game by game, week by week. We have suffered enough," he remarked. Stamford Bridge hoodoo finally broken Spurs arrived at Stamford Bridge with a dismal record, having won only once at the stadium since 1990—a 3-1 victory back in 2018. However, De Zerbi was adamant that his current group should not be burdened by the failures of their predecessors. He insisted that the focus remains entirely on the future and establishing a new identity for the North London outfit. "It’s not our responsibility the results of the past. Winning the game, we are very happy for them, very proud for the club. But I think we are working to change the mentality of our club in the last seasons," De Zerbi explained. item.title: Prairie View A&M uses big run to take control, beat East Texas A&M
item.description: A run of 24 consecutive points helped Prairie View A&M take control en route to a nonconference win over East Texas A&M. (Yi-Chin Lee, Houston Chronicle / Staff photographer) COMMERCE - Prairie View A&M made it consecutive wins, beating East Texas A&M 30-19 on Saturday night at Memorial Stadium. The Panthers (4-5) took control of the nonconference game against the Lions (2-6) of the Southland Conference by scoring 24 consecutive points after trailing 6-0. Tevin Carter threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns to Rodny Ojo while Chase Bingmon ran for 77 yards on nine carries, including two TDs, for Prairie View. Bingmon's 2-yard TD run early in the second quarter put the Panthers up for good. Carter and Ojo then connected for TDs sandwiched around an Ehtan Eddins field goal to put the Panthers up 24-6 early in the fourth quarter. The Lions drew within 24-19 with 9:39 left but Bingmon's 52-yard TD run just 52 seconds later iced the Panthers' win. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. This article originally published at Prairie View A&M uses big run to take control, beat East Texas A&M .

item.title: Maple Leafs Expose Real Oilers in Blowout Win
item.description: The Toronto Maple Leafs' blowout win on Saturday night at Rogers Place showed what the real Edmonton Oilers look like. Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs exposed the real Edmonton Oilers in a 7-2 blowout win at Rogers Place on Saturday night. Edmonton, with Connor McDavid’s insane point streak, has dominated their opponents this season. Well, that was not the case against Toronto. The Leafs opened up a 5-1 lead in the third period, capitalizing on just about every mistake the Oilers made on the night. But it wasn’t so much a question of taking advantage of mistakes. It was about shutting down the powerful Edmonton offense. Yes, Leon Draisaitl had two goals. Connor McDavid added two assists. But they were nearly as influential as they’ve been in other games. Plus, one of those patented desperate third-period comebacks that Edmonton has pulled off so many times did not come to fruition. The bottom line is that the Maple Leafs showed everyone that the Oilers have a fatal flaw, one that has followed them around for years: They don’t play defense. Auston Matthews’ tally was possible thanks to Easton Cowan making Ryan Shea look sick on the pass. MATTHEWS SNIPES IT AFTER A BEAUTY FEED FROM EASTON COWAN! pic.twitter.com/9Z0ZSmGBsp — Maple Leafs Hotstove (@LeafsNews) October 25, 2026 As for the goaltending, well, that wasn’t any better. Tristan Jarry gave up six on the night, including this headscratcher: Toronto goal! Scored by Zack MacEwen with 06:21 left in the 3rd. Assisted by Brandon Duhaime. EDM: 1 | TOR: 5 #TORvsEDM #LetsGoOilers #PassionNeverSleeps pic.twitter.com/rqfhPH0fMG — NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 25, 2026 The Maple Leafs showed on Saturday night that when the Oilers can’t outscore their opponents, they fold like a lawn chair. Toronto deserved to win. They were better in every facet of the game. Oilers too many passengers. Didn’t match Maple Leafs competitiveness tonight. — Jason Gregor (@JasonGregor) October 25, 2026 Maple Leafs Beat Oilers at Their Own Game The entire Oilers’ game plan hinges on puck possession and control. They use speed and transitions to move the puck up ice, often catching opponents flat-footed. When looking at many of McDavid’s goals, they start with a strong rush and someone crashing the net. Leon Draisaitl’s first of the night, scored while 4-on-4, was a good example of how they controlled the entire play, eventually leading to the tally. Edmonton goal! Scored by Leon Draisaitl with 00:56 left in the 2nd. Assisted by Connor McDavid and Evan Bouchard. EDM: 1 | TOR: 3 #TORvsEDM #LetsGoOilers #PassionNeverSleeps pic.twitter.com/kEeWvR1h4r — NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) October 25, 2026 The goal momentarily swung momentum in Edmonton’s favor. But it was the Maple Leafs’ strong start to the third period, with William Nylander’s power play goal essentially putting the kibosh on any comeback hopes. Toronto Played Best Game of the Season When the final buzzer sounded, the Maple Leafs had indeed played their best game of the

But it was the Maple Leafs’ strong start to the third period, with William Nylander’s power play goal essentially putting the kibosh on any comeback hopes. Toronto Played Best Game of the Season When the final buzzer sounded, the Maple Leafs had indeed played their best game of the season. The Buds managed to mitigate the damage by Draisaitl and McDavid, while exposing the weak defense and goaltending that has characterized the Edmonton Oilers for eons now. The Leafs were coming off a concerning, if entertaining win against the New York Rangers . But if there were any concerns about Toronto, their win on Saturday went a long way to quelling them. In fact, the pounding in Edmonton reinforces the 6-3 win against the Colorado Avalanche earlier this season. Even with multiple losses on the blue line, the Maple Leafs look like a solid defensive team, with offensive contributions coming up and down the lineup. The goals by MacEwan, Troy Stecher, and Vinni Lettieri underscore just how dangerously balanced Toronto is looking this season. Oh, and let’s not forget that Anthony Stolarz had a fantastic game. Stolarz stopped 30 of 32, doing his part to stifle Edmonton’s offense. The win also moved the Leafs into the top three in the Eastern Conference. Sure, it’s still early, but the rest of the Atlantic Division has to be on notice. item.title: Mitch Johnson admits what the Spurs must continue to do to maintain their winning form
item.description: Mitch Johnson admits what the Spurs must continue to do to maintain their winning form originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Antonio Spurs have finally ended their winless run to start the 2026-27 NBA season. They lost their first two games of the year, but they finally got a win on the board by beating the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday in a 122-106 victory. It was a much better effort from the Spurs compared to what they did against the Oklahoma City Thunder and the Houston Rockets . This was a well-rounded performance that head coach Mitch Johnson appreciates and would love to continue seeing moving forward. Mitch Johnson wants to keep seeing the Spurs fighting The Spurs have one of the most talented rosters in the NBA today, but they had a slow start to the season. Everyone knows that they are contenders now, so they have to meet sky-high expectations. However, they were quite disappointing in those first two games. Victor Wembanyama, in particular, had some bad performances. Since he is considered by a large chunk of the NBA community to be a favorite to get the MVP award, the win against the Mavericks was a return to form for the 7'5" behemoth. MORE: Dylan Harper believes the Spurs fans should calm down after a slow start to the 2026-27 season Johnson also wanted to highlight something that the Spurs did against the Mavericks that was absent in the first two games. That was the effort they put into the game with hustling for the ball, rebounding, defending, and many more. That was a big deal for Johnson, and he would prefer to keep that going. "Effort goes a long way. It's as simple as it sounds. As talented as these guys are, consistent effort with just a little bit of togetherness and execution can really be something to grow upon and build upon... We just have not been consistent enough in a lot of ways," Johnson said after the Spurs' win against the Mavericks . Johnson is ready to jumpstart the Spurs' campaign now with what he has seen. In preseason, Johnson said that the Spurs weren't ready just yet, but with the performnace against the Mavs, it seems that he unlocked something that will spell trouble for the rest of the league. item.title: 2022 Top 10 NBA Draft Pick Finds New Landing Spot While Thunder Open Two-Way By Waiving 2nd-Round Pick
item.description: New York Knicks forward Jeremy Sochan (20) attends practice during the NBA finals media day at Frost Bank Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor Jeremy Sochan has found a new home. Sochan was selected with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 G-League Draft by the Texas Legends earlier today. The Legends, the G-League affiliate of the Dallas Mavericks , are the 2022 Top 10 draft pick’s fourth franchise over the last year. Jeremy Sochan will be the No. 1 pick of the G League Draft, sources told @hoopshype. Sochan will join the Dallas Mavericks’ affiliate, Texas Legends, and attempt to work his way back to the NBA. He’s averaged 9.9 points and 5.4 rebounds in four seasons with the Spurs and Knicks. https://t.co/Yv3cEicO3b — Michael Scotto (@MikeAScotto) October 24, 2026 Jeremy Sochan Looking For Another Chance The Portland Trail Blazers waived Sochan on October 17. Sochan, who played for the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks last season, signed with the Trail Blazers in early August to compete for the team’s final roster spot. But the Blazers ultimately chose to leave the spot open, Sochan played well in his limited time with Portland this preseason. The 23-year-old forward compiled 3.6 points and 2.4 rebounds in 11 minutes with shooting splits of 49.6/24.4/73.1. He scored at least six points in three of his four outings. The Spurs drafted Sochan with the 9th overall pick in the 2022 draft after one season at Baylor. The 6-8 forward was a major part of the Spurs rotation in his first season. But he saw his role reduced last season as the Spurs upgraded their talent. Sochan saw action in 28 games, though he averaged just 12 minutes a contest for the Spurs last season before being waived. A few days after being waived by the Spurs, Sochan hooked up with the Knicks, who had an open roster spot. He saw limited time with the Knicks, including 26 minutes in eight postseason appearances. Sochan is a versatile defender with a high motor capable of guarding 3-5. Sochan is a strong rebounder and secondary playmaker who excels in transition. However, he is very limited offensively in the half-court and struggles shooting from beyond the arc. Oklahoma City Waives Otega Oweh The Oklahoma City Thunder have released Otega Oweh from his two-way contract as he suffered a season-ending Achilles injury during the preseason. The Thunder acquired the 23-year-old on day two of the draft from Miami for Ryan Conwell, the No. 37 pick. Oweh struggled shooting the ball during the Summer League. However, Oweh appeared in all four exhibition games and showed some of his all-around ability, posting a double-double against Atlanta. He’s averaged 9.9 points and 5.4 rebounds in four seasons with the Spurs and Knicks. https://t.co/Yv3cEicO3b — Michael Scotto (@MikeAScotto) October 24, 2026 Jeremy Sochan Looking For Another Chance The Portland Trail Blazers waived Sochan on October 17. Sochan, who played for the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks last season, signed with the Trail Blazers in early August to compete for the team’s final roster spot. But the Blazers ultimately chose to leave the spot open, Sochan played well in his limited time with Portland this preseason. The 23-year-old forward compiled 3.6 points and 2.4 rebounds in 11 minutes with shooting splits of 49.6/24.4/73.1. He scored at least six points in three of his four outings. The Spurs drafted Sochan with the 9th overall pick in the 2022 draft after one season at Baylor. The 6-8 forward was a major part of the Spurs rotation in his first season. But he saw his role reduced last season as the Spurs upgraded their talent. Sochan saw action in 28 games, though he averaged just 12 minutes a contest for the Spurs last season before being waived. A few days after being waived by the Spurs, Sochan hooked up with the Knicks, who had an open roster spot. He saw limited time with the Knicks, including 26 minutes in eight postseason appearances. Sochan is a versatile defender with a high motor capable of guarding 3-5. Sochan is a strong rebounder and secondary playmaker who excels in transition. However, he is very limited offensively in the half-court and struggles shooting from beyond the arc. Oklahoma City Waives Otega Oweh The Oklahoma City Thunder have released Otega Oweh from his two-way contract as he suffered a season-ending Achilles injury during the preseason. The Oklahoma City Thunder has waived guard Otega Oweh per Thunder PR — Andrew Schlecht (@AndrewKSchlecht) October 24, 2026 Oweh was selected with the No. 41 pick in this year’s draft and signed a two-way deal with the Thunder a few days after the draft. The Thunder acquired the 23-year-old on day two of the draft from Miami for Ryan Conwell, the No. 37 pick. Oweh struggled shooting the ball during the Summer League. However, Oweh appeared in all four exhibition games and showed some of his all-around ability, posting a double-double against Atlanta. He averaged 6.8 points on 40% shooting from the field and 5.0 rebounds in 24 minutes over four games before suffering an Achilles injury against the Pacers. The Thunder replace Otega Oweh with Micah Peavy Oklahoma City Thunder guard Otega Oweh (13) dribbles against Atlanta Hawks guard Nickeil Alexander-Walker (7) during the third quarter at State Farm Arena. Photo Credit: Jordan Godfree, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Thunder agreed to a two-way contract with Micah Peavy on Friday. So, it made sense with Oweh out for the season and his contract non-guaranteed for them to replace him. The Memphis Grizzlies waived Peavy on Monday after losing out in a competition for a spot on their final roster. The Grizzlies acquired Peavy and Jordan Hawkins from the Memphis Grizzlies for Taj Gibson and A.J. Johnson. Peavy played two preseason games with Memphis. The 25-year-old tallied 16 points on 6-of-11 shooting, five assists and two steals. He averaged 12.5 points, 3.0 assists, and 1.5 steals with 47.1/50.0/1.000/ Peavy spent all of last season with the New Orleans Pelicans after they acquired the No. 40 pick in 2025 from the Washington Wizards . While Peavy struggled to shoot, he scored in double figures 8 times in 61 games, topping 20 points twice. Peavy is a multi-positional wing defender with high motor skills. But his shooting is a big question mark. Minnesota Timberwolves guard Terrence Shannon Jr. (1) drives to the basket through New Orleans Pelicans guard Micah Peavy (14) in the second half at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Last Word on 2022 Top 10 NBA Draft Pick Finds New Landing Spot Sochan is headed to a rebuilding Mavericks organization that is 1-2 on the season and dealing with several injuries. Kyrie Irving , Cooper Flagg , Caleb Martin, Tarik Biberovic , Santi Aldama and Dereck Lively II are the injured players. So, while Sochan has to prove he is still an NBA player with the Legends, he is in an ideal spot to get another chance, as the Mavs are projected to struggle this entire season. Unfortunately, Oweh suffered a season-ending injury, but it made sense that the Thunder felt the need to replace him, as it is a long season since his contract is non-guaranteed and doesn’t count against the cap. Peavy is a strong fit for the Thunder, as he is a defense-centric wing with upside and just the type of prospect that general manager Sam Presti likes. He joins Josh Dix and Brooks Barnhizer . More News Hornets vs. Heat: Prediction and Preview 2027 NBA Draft Prospect Preview: Arkansas Razorbacks’ Jordan Smith Jr. What To Make Of The Sacramento Kings’ 0-2 Start To The Season Photo Credit: Dustin Safranek, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect

item.title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson; Tyler Huntley to start vs. Bengals
item.description: Oct 11, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley (5) celebrates with quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) after a touchdown during overtime against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens downgraded quarterback Lamar Jackson’s status from ‘questionable’ to ‘out’ ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Backup Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will make his third straight start after an overtime win over the Falcons and a disappointing loss to the Browns. Jackson’s comments on Friday, as well as his limited practice participation all week, portended this outcome. He revealed that he suffered a high ankle sprain and was struggling to put weight on his left leg when running. He indicated that he did not need to be 100% to take the field, but emphasized that he would be doing a “disservice” to his team if he plays before his body is ready. Downgrading Jackson’s status is reminiscent of the lead-up to last year’s Week 8 matchup against the Bears. He suffered a hamstring injury three weeks prior and returned to practice with limited-limited-full participation days and a questionable designation on the injury report. However, Jackson did not speak to media that week, and the team only changed his status after reports emerged that he was not expected to play. This year, Jackson provided rare clarity regarding his injury, answering over a dozen questions about his status. Despite his multiple references to a “grace period” before making a decision, it was clear that he was not ready to play as of Friday. Rapid improvements in time for a Sunday afternoon kickoff were never likely. Saturday’s reports also characterized Jackson as a game-time decision. The differences from last year’s approach should ensure the Ravens avoid another league investigation that resulted in a $100,000 fine. At face value, it seems unclear why the Ravens had to update Jackson’s status on Saturday, especially if he is in that 50-50 range. Baltimore has let plenty of other players go through a pregame workout and announced their status via the inactive list 90 minutes before kickoff. It would actually benefit the team to force their opponents to prepare for Jackson to start and sit. But a two-time MVP moves betting lines, and the league is inextricably tied with sportsbooks. If Jackson is not playing, that information (from their perspective) has to be made public.

item.title: O’Shaquie Foster Freezes Out Emanuel Navarrete Saturday
item.description: What to Know In a dominant and driven performance, O’Shaquie Foster froze out Emanuel Navarrete, becoming the unified super featherweight champion in San Antonio on Saturday Foster dropped Navarrete three times in the final round to seal his impressive victory. In the co-main event, Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez made his case as the 2026 Prospect of the Year. We’re believers. What to Know Three belts will be on the line in a sensational super featherweight unification fight between Emanual Navarrete and O’Shaquie Foster Saturday at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. In the co-feature, undefeated prospect Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez will take on two-time world title challenger Edward Vazquez The fight card airs on DAZN Boxing with the main card at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Before the bell action starts at 5:30 p.m. ET/2:30 p.m. PT. on DAZN, Top Rank and DAZN’s YouTube channels, and the Top Rank Classics FAST channel on Roku, Tubi, Pluto and Vizio. O’Shaquie Foster dared to put his hand on a hot stove Saturday, but by the force of his will and skill, he put Emanuel Navarrete into a deep freeze. O’Shaquie Foster made a serious bid as the 2026 Fighter of the Year with a cool as ice performance over Emanuel Navarrete Saturday. Photo: Top Rank Boxing In nothing less than a tour de force, Foster of Orange, Texas (26-3, 12 KOs) confronted the offense of Navarrete of Mexico (40-3-1, 33 KOs) head on with a fearless determination, disarming him and eventually wearing him down. After scoring three knockdowns in the final round, not even the Texas judges could mess this one up. Two judges got it right at 118-108, with a third seeing it at 115-111. Foster wins the IBF and WBO titles from Navarrete, and the vacant Ring Magazine belt, while defending his WBC World Featherweight title. “There was no way they could rob me. I controlled every round … I knew I was doing the most work in there,” said Foster. I knew he was gonna be awkward. He’s a great champion. I just had a little bit more in me tonight,” said Foster. Navarrete was equally gracious toward the new unified champion. “What I have to say, it’s short, acceptable, and it’s professional. In this sport, it’s about styles. In the co-main event, Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez made his case as the 2026 Prospect of the Year. We’re believers. What to Know Three belts will be on the line in a sensational super featherweight unification fight between Emanual Navarrete and O’Shaquie Foster Saturday at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. In the co-feature, undefeated prospect Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez will take on two-time world title challenger Edward Vazquez The fight card airs on DAZN Boxing with the main card at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Before the bell action starts at 5:30 p.m. ET/2:30 p.m. PT. on DAZN, Top Rank and DAZN’s YouTube channels, and the Top Rank Classics FAST channel on Roku, Tubi, Pluto and Vizio. O’Shaquie Foster dared to put his hand on a hot stove Saturday, but by the force of his will and skill, he put Emanuel Navarrete into a deep freeze. O’Shaquie Foster made a serious bid as the 2026 Fighter of the Year with a cool as ice performance over Emanuel Navarrete Saturday. Photo: Top Rank Boxing In nothing less than a tour de force, Foster of Orange, Texas (26-3, 12 KOs) confronted the offense of Navarrete of Mexico (40-3-1, 33 KOs) head on with a fearless determination, disarming him and eventually wearing him down. After scoring three knockdowns in the final round, not even the Texas judges could mess this one up. Two judges got it right at 118-108, with a third seeing it at 115-111. Foster wins the IBF and WBO titles from Navarrete, and the vacant Ring Magazine belt, while defending his WBC World Featherweight title. “There was no way they could rob me. I controlled every round … I knew I was doing the most work in there,” said Foster. SHOCK DROPS NAVARRETE IN THE FINAL ROUND! ⚡ #NavarreteFoster | Live NOW on DAZN ▪️ https://t.co/GxztAYcmYt — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 25, 2026 “I worked so hard to get here, man,” said a smiling Foster. “I knew he was gonna be strong. I knew he was gonna be awkward. He’s a great champion. I just had a little bit more in me tonight,” said Foster. Navarrete was equally gracious toward the new unified champion. “What I have to say, it’s short, acceptable, and it’s professional. In this sport, it’s about styles. His style was better than mine tonight. He won tonight. Everyone, please applaud for him,” said Navarrete to his many fans in San Antonio. Foster Shows He’s More Than a Tactical Genius O’Shaquie Foster had more than enough firepower and was willing to use it to keep Emanuel Navarrete at bay. Photo: Top Rank Boxing Navarrete said he knew fans didn’t want to see a defensive fight. Given Foster’s superior technical skills, fans expected him to slow the pace and fight Navarrete at a safe distance, given his exceptional ring IQ, defense, and hand-and-foot speed. Foster and his trainer Bobby Benton must have realized he had the skills to engage with Navarrete and disarm him as the savvy ring general who is cool under fire. He stood his ground with confidence and healthy defiance, proving critics wrong in predicting he wouldn’t try to engage Navarrete in a firefight. “He’s an awkward, strong champion. Man, it was a long night. He’s got heavy hands. But I’ve got a chin, and I’m not really worried about power. I’ve got my own,” said Foster. Foster’s knockout rate is deceiving. He doesn’t always need to move in to stop the fight. But on Saturday after the 11 th round, Benton encouraged Foster to go for it. The three knockdowns didn’t end in a knockout, but they left an undeniable mark on the performance. “I felt like I was breaking him down. I wanted him to overwork, played a little mind games with him. Coming into the fight I knew I was going to be able to run him into shots, and that’s what I did.” O’Shaquie Foster scored three knockdowns in the final round to seal his victory. Photo: Top Rank Boxing Foster reflected on his accomplishment, something ten years in the making, after being incarcerated, then deciding to pursue boxing and stick with it after several early career losses. Now, Foster and trainer Bobby Benton have legitimate claims as possible 2026 Fighter and Trainer of the Year. “Words can’t even explain. It took a lot of work, a lot of sacrifice, and a lot of belief, especially where I’ve come from. “I want to go undisputed, man. My dream is to become undisputed and make history. All I need is one more to fulfill my biggest dream and then see Shakur,” said Foster. Boxing fans are already anticipating that all-American showdown. Foster’s priority is the winner of the December 19 fight in Belfast between WBA World Super Featherweight champion Anthony Cacace and former champion Nick Ball. But before any of this happens, remember that the WBO granted Navarrete the unification bout with Foster on the condition that the winner defend the WBO title against Charly Suarez of the Philippines within 180 days. Garner holds the WBC interim title, while Zaurbek won the IBF eliminator. Chop Chop Gonzalez Ready To Rumble With the Champions Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez made his case as 2026 Prospect of the Year. Photo: Top Rank Boxing Unbeaten featherweight Albert “Chop Chop” Gonzalez of Moreno Valley, California expected to face a test against Fort Worth native and former two-time world title challenger Edward Vazquez of Fort Worth, Texas . Ummm, things didn’t exactly work out that way. Uno, dos, adios. ALBERT CHOP CHOP GONZALEZ GETS IT DONE IN 2 ROUNDS! 😱 #NavarreteFoster | Live NOW on DAZN ▪️ https://t.co/rmk7S5Wj8k — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 25, 2026 Gonzalez (19-0, 12 KOs) landed 28 power shots out of 53 landed punches in four minutes. Almost half went to the body of Vazquez of Fort Worth, Texas (20-4, 6 KOs) . Vazquez came out aggressively but landed only nine punches on Gonzalez before being dropped. Consider this: the only other opponent to stop Vazquez, featherweight world champion Rafael “Divino” Espinoza, needed seven rounds to stop Vazquez on body shots in May 2025. “I wanted to stay in the pocket a little bit, see what his pressure choices were, and when I seen he was a little slow in the pocket, I knew I could catch him in between the shots and land that body shot,” said Gonzalez. “The body’s on my mind every single fight.” Gonzalez said he was surprised when Vazquez couldn’t beat the count of referee Laurence Cole, but said it would have only delayed the same result. Gonzalez mentioned that he’d be willing to join trainer Robert Garcia in traveling to Riyadh, where WBC champion Rafael “El Divino” Espinoza’s original opponent dropped out. But Chop Chop won’t get his chance. A replacement is already scheduled. Gonzalez credited Robert Garcia and the entire RGBA team for his four-fight knockout streak . With Saturday’s win, Gonzalez jumped to the top of our 2026 Prospect of the Year list. Frank Martin Finding His Way Back Frank Martin pinned an elusive Tarik Zaina in the corner and left his left hook do the work. Photo: Top Rank Boxing Super lightweight contender Frank Martin of Indianapolis (20-1-1, 14 KOs) faced a tricky opponent and a solid game plan as he returned to the ring on Saturday. Tarik Zaina of Morocco (18-4-1, 12 KOs), who trains in Tijuana, Mexico, said Martin was the opponent he always wanted to face. In the early rounds, it was easy to see why. Zaina used his reach and movement to frustrate Martin early. The San Antonio fans began to boo, unhappy about the lack of serious action. Eventually Martin settled in, settled down, and didn’t get anxious. He figured out how to handle Zaina. It paid off with a sensational seventh-round TKO win. From ringside 😱 @TheGhost_2016 | @DAZNBoxing https://t.co/j7LxIyRovx — Top Rank Boxing (@trboxing) October 25, 2026 Martin caught Zaina with a solid left hook count

item.title: Why Pat McAfee apologised to Nick Saban for ‘ruining the whole sport’ on College Gameday
item.description: Photo by Ella Hall/LSU/University Images via Getty Images "} Pat McAfee addressed legendary coach Nick Saban when he went off about all the criticism he has received for his signature move on College GameDay. Pat McAfee has become one of the most famous sports personalities in the country in recent years. He has become one of the faces of ESPN’s College GameDay as well, alongside fellow analysts like Kirk Herbstreit and legendary college coach Nick Saban. One of McAfee’s signature moves on the show has been taking his shirt off upon urging from the crowds at the various college football games they go to. This weekend, the crew was in Salt Lake City, Utah ahead of the Utes-Cougars clash. Pat had a point to make, it would seem, and he addressed Saban while doing so. Pat McAfee called out NYT again while taking his shirt off, jokingly saying sorry for ‘ruining the sport’ McAfee’s exuberance is what makes him endearing to a lot of fans, but it is also what has earned him some detractors. His tendency to create a spectacle out of himself has been criticised by some, including the New York Times, and there are those who would prefer for the focus to stay on the game. It seems McAfee is not a fan of being called out. Because after he initially said he wouldn’t take his shirt off this time, that’s exactly what he did. He then threw a jab at NYT while talking to Saban. “New York Times already saying it,” McAfee said during College GameDay . “This a****** is shirtless at 9:02 a.m. Eastern. Sorry, Coach. I’m ruining the whole sport. I’m ruining the whole sport because of this. I just enjoy it too much not to have a good time.” McAfee is unlikely to stop doing what is clearly so popular among the crowds he performs most often in front of. His apology was obviously a dig at his critics more so than being genuine. This seems like a battle McAfee will be fighting for some time. item.title: Adri Mehmeti outshines Lionel Messi as New York Red Bulls upset Inter Miami in tight MLS playoff chase
item.description: Adri Mehmeti outshines Lionel Messi as New York Red Bulls upset Inter Miami in tight MLS playoff chase originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . HARRISON, N.J. — Fans flocked to Sports Illustrated Stadium on Saturday evening to be wowed by Lionel Messi . Instead, they were treated to the Adri Mehmeti show. The 17-year-old American kid outshined the greatest player of all-time as the New York Red Bulls overwhelmed Inter Miami 2-0 to secure a massive three points in the MLS playoff race. From the opening whistle, the Red Bulls pressed the Herons into oblivion, forcing an early own-goal off Casemiro and missing a host of other clear-cut chances created directly off turnovers. Through it all, Mehmeti was central to their ability to overwhelm the visitors in midfield. In the first 15 minutes of the match, Inter Miami held 72 percent possession, but played practically the entire time in their own half, unable to get out of jail while being overwhelmed on the ball. That continued all first half, as the visitors could not string anything cohesive together and were routinely caught out and countered. It was a team effort from the hosts, truly, but Mehmeti's influence in midfield was undeniable. "We hope it was a spectacle in the most positive sense," said Red Bulls head coach Michael Bradley after the game. "We understand the responsibility that, on certain nights, when certain teams come here with certain players, the spotlights come on a little brighter. That's our chance to show we have a pretty good team too." It was Mehmeti, not Messi, who snatched the spotlight. Having just accepted the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports out in Spain just two days prior, Messi did not start the match. As Inter Miami floundered throughout the first half and into the early part of the second half, the hugely pro-Miami crowd repeatedly chanted his name, hoping for their Argentine legend to come save the day. But even when he came on just past the hour mark, to great cheers and elation — the loudest the crowd was all evening — he was ineffective, hemmed in by the Red Bulls and left on an island with little help. That had everything to do with Mehmeti. Playing alongside Ghanan international Mohammed Sofo, who was moved from his usual No. 10 position into a dual No. 8 role alongside Mehmeti, the American youngster shined throughout the match. Mehmeti led the Red Bulls with 82 touches and 55 accurate passes in his 85 minutes, able to keep Inter Miami's possession in front of him almost the entire way through. "What else can I say?" asked Sofo of his midfield partner Mehmeti, "I mean, when you look at the quality he has, especially his age also, it's unbelievable. "Since I switched my position to No. 8, I think our connection has been amazing so far. I just hope we can play more games together. "The maturity he has is unbelievable," Sofo said. "The vision he has, he knows when to play forward, when to c

"What else can I say?" asked Sofo of his midfield partner Mehmeti, "I mean, when you look at the quality he has, especially his age also, it's unbelievable. "Since I switched my position to No. 8, I think our connection has been amazing so far. I just hope we can play more games together. "The maturity he has is unbelievable," Sofo said. "The vision he has, he knows when to play forward, when to calm down. Sometimes he does things I'm like 'wow.' For me, as a No. 8 or also as a No. 10, I try to find myself in the pockets, and sometimes he finds me with just two touches. Other players need to take a first touch, look for it, and then play it. But for him, he can just...second touch, he finds you." It was the culmination of all of Mehmeti's best skill sets — passing, positioning, range, ball-stopping, and pressing — that came together on one evening to allow him to boss the match. Adri Mehmeti just toying with a World Cup winner in Rodrigo De Paul here 🇺🇸 Only a matter of time until Mehmeti is getting a real run with the USMNT. Just 17. https://t.co/c3wvf85kGY — Joseph Lowery (@joeclowery) October 24, 2026 "For a young player, Adri has...really good starting points," Bradley told reporters after the match. "He has personality, he has technical ability — the technical ability that you need to play in that spot when spaces are tight and things happen fast — he has a feel and understanding for the game, and the way things have gone this year, we've thrown an incredible amount at him. "I didn't know coming into the season what exactly it was going to mean for Adri," the Red Bulls' coach continued. "We knew that they [the young players] were going to be a real part of the first team, and in the end we were going to see how it played out — how they responded every day, how they took to ideas, how they pushed themselves along in a group, how they earned respect. "We have put a lot on Adri's plate. We expect a lot of him, he has a lot of responsibility in our team for a 17-year-old and he doesn't bat an eye." USMNT fans got a taste of what Mehmeti can bring to the midfield during the latest international break, but it was still just that — a taste. He played a total of 80 minutes across his first three international caps, 62 of which came in the 4-2 win over Chile. This match tonight against Messi and company was vintage Mehmeti, if such thing for a teenager exists. He dazzled on the ball, passed to every corner of the pitch, completed both his tackles, and led all outfield players in the match with 10 recoveries, tied with World Cup winner Rodrigo De Paul. By the end of the game, FotMob’s statistical algorithm had named Mehmeti as Man of the Match, while he had the second-highest individual rating on SofaScore behind the nonsensically high number for Inter Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair. The win was huge for the Red Bulls, who are teetering on the cusp of the MLS playoff cut line. The three points moved them back onto solid ground — only just — as they reclaimed the ninth spot in the Eastern Conference, the final postseason position. With just three matches remaining, the race is incredibly tight. With 39 points, the Red Bulls are just one point ahead of the Columbus Crew and three clear of Toronto. Meanwhile, FC Cincinnati and Orlando City each sit on 42 points just above hem in seventh and eighth. "Obviously you knew when you win balls in dangerous spots that there's going to be space, and we were able to take that space and capitalize on it and make good chances to score the two goals," Mehmeti said after the match. "We played our football with our ideas, and the way the guys just kept on going, kept pushing through, even when they [Inter Miami] had long spells of possession, was great. So yea, it was a really good performance, and we go on to the next one." On the national team level, the star of 17-year-old sensation Cavan Sullivan has risen exponentially in recent months, and he stands to be an exciting player for the USMNT in the coming years, but Mehmeti might be the most important young player in the talent pool. He will have his work cut out for him breaking into a national team midfield that boasts the likes of Weston McKennie, Tyler Adams, Johnny Cardoso, Sebastian Berhalter, and Gio Reyna, but fans hope he can be the anchor of the next generation of midfield talent. There's a long way to go for that to happen, but on the pitch in Harrison, New Jersey tonight, he stole the show from the greatest of all-time. That, at the very least, is something to get very excited about.

item.title: 4 Lafayette area volleyball teams take home regional championships
item.description: MONTICELLO — One of the only three teams that beat No. 7 (4A) Harrison volleyball in the regular season, No. 2 Westfield, was the team the Raiders were going to have to beat to win the regional championship Saturday, Oct. 24, at Twin Lakes High School. Despite giving the Rocks a battle in the second set, the result was the same. Harrison fell in a 3-0 sweep (25-12, 25-21, 25-15), concluding a year for the program that brought its fourth consecutive sectional championship win. “Just even from last year to this season is the trust and commitment and family that they were on the court,” coach Jacklyn Lehe of the team’s growth. “I wish we could’ve fought just a little bit harder (Saturday), but I have a great group of girls.” More: Rossville volleyball stuns No 1 Covington, repeats as regional champion More: Faith Christian boys soccer's postseason run ends with crushing loss The postseason hopes ran deep for the Raiders heading into the tournament. Ending the season with 19 straight wins, they dominated most of their slate. But Westfield (27-2) presented a different challenge than most of the opponents they’ve countered, carrying size and speed across the board that was tough to match up against. Harrison has had to rely on its youth all season. It only has four seniors on the roster, three of which have been unavailable for the postseason, and 10 of its 15 players are underclassmen. But even with that inexperience, they’ve stepped up throughout the sectional run and gave the Rocks a battle in several pockets of Saturday’s loss. “We gave it our all. Every practice, every ball we had,” sophomore Gia Stokes said. “It sucks with our situation, the three seniors gone, I think the underclassmen did a really good job stepping it up and the ability for them to come off and play against a fast-paced Westfield team … is just awesome.” The outlook for the Raiders is bright with their youth, as disappointing as the end of the year was. Stokes became a team captain this season and had a team-high of 363 kills coming into the game. Freshman Story Nixon blossomed at setter with 894 assists. Stella Snider will be a leading senior for the squad and development should continue with other returners and emerging freshmen that come up. Stokes became a team captain this season and had a team-high of 363 kills coming into the game. Freshman Story Nixon blossomed at setter with 894 assists. She’s been with Lehe since she took the job four years ago, and watching her and the rest of the seniors grow has made that batch a special group for Lehe that’s bittersweet to see leave. In the locker room before the Raiders headed home, Stokes told her teammates to “be leaders.” Her and the rest of class may be gone, but being a leader by example is something that they hope to pass down. “We’re going to have a lot of sophomores and juniors next year,” Lehe said, “But I think they can do it because they had a great role model to show them the way.” And the players themselves believe that, too. We’re going to be able to compete with the bigger Indy teams.” West Lafayette sweeps Leo While Harrison's season ended, others around the Lafayette area extended theirs. West Lafayette (21-12) approached this week’s matchup with Leo feeling confident that they could breakthrough the regional round, and that they did. It’s their first regional championship since 2021. West Lafayette defeated Leo 3-0 (25-21, 25-22, 25-11). Between sectionals and regionals, it still has yet to drop a single set to an opponent. At the Northwood semi-state bracket, the Red Devils will take on West Noble (30-3) in the second semifinal at 12:30 p.m. Saturday, Oct. 31. A win would send them to the semi-state championship match later that night at 7 p.m. Benton Central takes down Muncie Burris In Class 2A, the Bison (24-6) went back-to-back in the regional championship, defeating Muncie Burris (24-6) in a 3-1 (23-25, 32-20, 25-23, 25-17) win. Benton Central will face Oak Hill (24-8) in the Peru semi-state bracket as it seeks to make the state championship game in Class 2A once again. That match will be at 10 a.m. Saturday, Oct. 31, with the potential title game at 6 p.m. Rossville, South Newton advance in 1A Rossville (26-7) completed a 3-2 (23-25, 17-25, 25-18, 26-24, 21-19) comeback win over the No. 1 (1A) Trojans (31-4) to go back-to-back in the regional championship. Meanwhile, South Newton won a five-set thriller over No. 4 Marquette Catholic (25-27, 25-20, 25-22, 24-26, 15-13). Both teams are on opposite sides of the 1A semi-state draw at Delphi, which means they could face each other in the championship with semifinal wins. item.title: William Nylander Reaches Historic Goal Milestone for Maple Leafs
item.description: Maple Leafs William Nylander Getty Toronto Maple Leafs forward William Nylander scored his 300th goal during the Maple Leafs’ win on Saturday night. The Maple Leafs routed the Edmonton Oilers 7-2 in a blowout win on Saturday night for Toronto, who have won four straight games and are looking every bit like a playoff contender at the moment. Nylander scored twice for Toronto, once on the power play and once into an empty net, as Toronto once again gave Edmonton problems at Rogers Place, an arena where they have had plenty of success. William Nylander Reaches 300-Goal Mark After scoring his 299th and 300th career goal, Nylander reached a very elite group of Maple Leafs players who have reached that milestone with the historic hockey club. THAT'S 300 CAREER GOALS FOR WILLIAM NYLANDER 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/AuXRlPQ72h — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 25, 2026 Nylander’s two goals gave him eight for the year as he is on pace for another 40-goal season for the fourth time in his NHL career. He also has 18 points this season. William Nylander’s Maple Leafs Career Nylander was drafted by Toronto with the eighth overall pick in the 2014 NHL Entry Draft, and he has spent his entire NHL career with the Maple Leafs since then. In 763 career regular-season games, Nylander has scored 300 goals and 709 points, while also adding 26 goals and 58 points in 62 career postseason games. The Maple Leafs haven’t had much playoff success during Nylander’s tenure with the club, but it hasn’t been his fault, as he has been playing so well for the club over the years. This season is make-or-break for the Maple Leafs in many ways, as the team is trying to prove to captain Auston Matthews that they are a legitimate Stanley Cup contender and that he should re-sign with the team on a contract extension before his deal with the franchise runs out after next season. Based on how well Toronto has been playing so far this season, it’s fair to say that the Maple Leafs are back, and having Nylander scoring so many goals for the team is certainly helping them, as he is one of the Maple Leafs’ best players and has been ever since he first entered the team’s lineup in 2015. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post William Nylander Reaches Historic Goal Milestone for Maple Leafs appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Loss to Flames Shows Gibson Not off to Hot Start
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Red Wings points-streak came to an end tonight with the Calgary Flames putting three second period goals on John Gibson and the Red Wings’ head tonight, beating them in regulation. It wasn’t Gibson’s prettiest outing, with the veteran netminder giving up four goals on the night in his likely last night at the Saddledome as the Red Wings for the first time since 2023, lost to the Flames 4-1. In a lather Last year, the Red Wings relied heavily on current Columbus Blue Jackets backup Cam Talbot for much of the first two months of the season as Gibson, newly acquired from Anaheim, adjusted to the team in front of him to begin the year. From December on, the Red Wings almost exclusively played Gibson however, with the-then 31-year-old netminder playing the third most games in a single season of his career (57) by the end of the year. Detroit has started Gibson in eight of their first eleven games, with the former Anaheim Ducks netminder accruing a .871 sv%, 3.35 GAA stat line going into the matchup with the Flames. With Gibson in net, the Red Wings are 3-4-1, and in two of those wins have needed to score 3 or more goals in order to achieve victory. “We don’t survive those moments. We don’t score enough, and tonight proved it.” Head coach Todd McLellan said. The Red Wings offensive attack, however, has not been their calling card so far this season, with Detroit relying heavily on team defense to keep them in games. There’s not much Gibson can do about the rest of the skaters on the team putting pucks in net, but he is ranked 52nd amongst NHL netminders in goals saved above expected on the year so far. Hold your horses Backup Daniil Tarasov tweaked something earlier on the Red Wings Pacific Division road trip, which leaves rookie Michal Postava , recalled under emergency conditions, as the Red Wings only other option aside from Gibson for the near future. The Red Wings will next find themselves facing off against the Edmonton Oilers and more importantly, Connor McDavid and Leon Draisatl. McDavid has 33 points in eleven games, and Draisatl is no slouch either, with 23. It would also be Gibson’s third straight start within the last week, if the Red Wings give him the nod. On the other hand, throwing Postava into his first start, on the road, against a high powered Oilers squad seems more like the stuff out of a goalie’s nightmare, though Postava has shown in the past that he is willing to meet just about any challenge. Either way, the Red Wings need to find a better balance in net for Gibson to find his footing. The Red Wings simply do not have the margin for error to be throwing away the first two months of the season waiting for him to find his late season form. item.title: Can players outside Europe win the Ballon d'Or? How France Football award eligibility works
item.description: Can players outside Europe win the Ballon d'Or? How France Football award eligibility works originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Every year, the Ballon d'Or is given out to the greatest football player from the previous season, awarded to the individual who displays the most exemplary performance across the entirety of the criteria period. Traditionally an award for European players from European nations, the eligibility for those who can win the Ballon d'Or has been questioned in recent years, as the talent base spreads further across the globe. Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal, and Kylian Mbappe are the frontrunners to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but there are nominees from all around the globe. The Sporting News brings you an overview at who is eligible to win the Ballon d'Or, football's most prestigious individual trophy, and what the history of the award is with regards to geography. MORE: All 30 Ballon d'Or nominees for the 2026 award Who is eligible to win the Ballon d'Or? Beginning with the award's inception in 1956, only players from European nations contracted to European clubs were eligible to win the Ballon d'Or. However, that restrictive nature has evolved over the years to the more inclusive award seen today. In 1995, the Ballon d'Or opened the nominee pool up to players of any nation playing for a European club. Then in 2007, all players in professional football around the world became eligible to win the award. In practice, however, the prize still remains locked into European-based players. Those clubs are not only the most visible but also the most prestigious, and thus performance at the highest level in Europe places players on a pedestal above all others. To date, no player contracted to a club outside of Europe has ever won the Ballon d'Or. The closest was Lionel Messi who secured the final Ballon d'Or of his career in 2023. While he accepted the award as an Inter Miami player, the voting period only considered the time during which he played his final year for Paris Saint-Germain. Thus, this does not officially count, but many still consider it as such. MORE: All-time list of Ballon d'Or winners: Who has won the most? | Which club has the most Ballon d'Or winners? Nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or The men's Ballon d'Or nominees for 2026 are as follows. Those playing for clubs outside Europe are italicized .
