Player Team(s) Career nominations Jude Bellingham Real Madrid / England 4 Pau Cubarsi Barcelona / Spain 1 Marc Cucurella Chelsea/Real Madrid / Spain 1 Ousmane Dembele Paris Saint-Germain / France 2 Luis Diaz Bayern Munich / Colombia 2 Bruno Fernandes Manchester United / Portugal 2 Erling Haaland Manchester City / Norway 6 Gabriel Arsenal / Brazil 1 Harry Kane Bayern Munich / England 8 Achraf Hakimi Paris Saint-Germain / Morocco 2 Lamine Yamal Barcelona / Spain 3 Khvicha Kvaratskhelia Paris Saint-Germain / Georgia 3 Marquinhos Paris Saint-Germain / Brazil 2 Sadio Mane Al Nassr / Senegal 5 Lisandro Martinez Inter Milan / Argentina 5 Kylian Mbappe Real Madrid / France 9 Nuno Mendes Paris Saint-Germain / Portugal 2 Lionel Messi Inter Miami / Argentina 17 Michael Olise Bayern Munich / France 2 Joao Neves Paris Saint-Germain / Portugal 2 William Pacho Paris Saint-Germain / Ecuador 1 Julian Quinones Al-Qadsiah / Mexico 1 Declan Rice Arsenal / England 3 Rodri Man City/Barcelona / Spain 3 Fabian Ruiz Paris Saint-Germain / Spain 2 Ferran Torres Barcelona/PSG / Spain 1 William Saliba Arsenal / France 2 Dayot Upamecano Bayern Munich / France 1 Vinicius Junior Real Madrid / Brazil 5 Vitinha Paris Saint-Germain / Portugal 3 The women's Ballon d'Or nominees for 2026 are as follows. Those playing for clubs outside Europe are italicized . Player Team(s) Career nominations Selma Bacha OL Lyonnes / France 2 Barbra Banda Orlando Pride / Zambia 3 Klara Buhl Bayern Munich / Germany 2 Esmee Brugts Barcelona / Netherlands 1 Mariona Caldentey Arsenal / Spain 3 Scarlett Camberos Club America / Mexico 1 Kerstin Casparij Manchester City / Netherlands 1 Temwa Chawinga Kansas City Current / Malawi 2 Cata Coll Barcelona / Spain 1 Melchie Dumornay OL Lyonnes / Haiti 2 Caroline Graham Hansen Barcelona / Norway 3 Alex Greenwood Manchester City / England 1 Patri Guijarro Barcelona / Spain 4 Pernille Harder Bayern Munich / Denmark 5 Yui Hasegawa Manchester City / Japan 3 Rose Lavelle Gotham City / USWNT 2 Mapi Leon Barcelona/London City Lionesses / Spain 2 Lorena Kanas City Current / Brazil 1 Melvine Malard Manchester United/Chelsea / France 1 Manaka Matsukubo North Carolina Courage/Chelsea / Japan 1 Ewa Pajor Barcelona / Poland 4 Vivianne Miedema Manchester City / Netherlands 4 Claudia Pina Barcelona / Spain 2 Alexia Putellas Barcelona/London City Lionesses 5 Alessia Russo Arsenal / England 2 Momoko Tanikawa Bayern Munich / Japan 1 Wendie Renard OL Lyonnes / France 6 Khadija Shaw Manchester City / Jamaica 3 Caroline Weir Real Madrid/OL Lyonnes / Scotland 2 Tessa Wullaert Inter Milan/Como / Belgium 1 How is the Ballon d'Or decided? Explaining criteria There are three main criteria that France Football has instructed voters to consider when crafting their list of potential winners: Individual performance, decisive impact, and impressive character Team achievements and collective success Sportsmanship and the player's class, on and off the pitch This means that not only does an individual's raw output matter, but also how well they contribute to their team's collective success, and the manner in which they conduct themselves. What is NOT meant to be considered is past achievements or global status. Thus, players who have won the award before are not supposed to be given a higher platform simply because of career success beyond the indicated time period. The Ballon d'Or, in theory, is meant simply to recognize the best player from the given time period and nothing more. That given time period has changed in recent years, however. Originally meant to produce the best player from the last calendar year, France Football recently changed the consideration timeframe to fit the European season. Thus, consideration is taken from the start of August through the end of the competitive summer tournaments. For the 2025/26 season, that means the consideration period begins at the start of league campaigns in August 2025 and runs through the end of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

item.title: Brentford XI vs Hull City – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Brentford XI vs Hull City – Predicted lineup and team news Brentford travel to the MKM Stadium on Sunday afternoon looking to bounce back from their first defeat of the season, a 2-1 loss to Liverpool that cost them two midfielders to red cards. Keith Andrews’ side are sixth in the Premier League with 10 points from seven matches, one point above Sunday’s hosts. Brentford remain unbeaten on their travels this season, though all three of their away matches so far have ended in draws. Brentford’s 13 goals scored and five-goal positive difference from seven matches are among the better underlying numbers in the division outside the top six. Brentford team news Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt are both suspended after being sent off in last weekend’s defeat to Liverpool, forcing Andrews to completely rebuild his central midfield pairing. Joshua Dasilva (hamstring), Kaye Furo (foot) and Antoni Milambo (knock) are also unavailable, with no fresh doubts reported elsewhere in the squad. Andrews will be without his first-choice central pairing for the first time this season, a blow against a Hull side that has scored three goals from high turnovers in the final third. Club-record signing Mamadou Sangare is set to take one of the vacant central midfield positions, in what will be his first Premier League start since 12 September. Mathias Jensen is expected to partner him in the middle of the park. Jaidon Anthony, Mikkel Damsgaard and Kevin Schade, who has scored three goals from 17 shots this season, are set to continue as the attacking trio behind Igor Thiago, with Michael Kayode and Keane Lewis-Potter retaining their places at full-back either side of Kristoffer Ajer and Schuster in central defence. Brentford predicted lineup Brentford possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Kelleher; Kayode, Schuster, Ajer, Lewis-Potter; Jensen, Sangare; Anthony, Damsgaard, Schade; Thiago When will the match kick off? The Premier League match kicks off at 14:00 BST on Sunday, 25 October 2026. How to watch Hull City vs Brentford? The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK. item.title: Liverpool vs Brighton – Match preview and team news
item.description: Liverpool vs Brighton – Match preview and team news Liverpool host Brighton & Hove Albion in a Premier League Gameweek 8 fixture at Anfield on Sunday, 25 October 2026. Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool are fifth in the table with 12 points from seven matches, four points and two places behind Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton in third. Brighton have won five of their seven league games, scoring 23 goals and conceding just five, and arrive on the back of a 5-0 win over Crystal Palace. Liverpool’s last meeting with Brighton ended in a 2-1 defeat at the Amex Stadium in March, Danny Welbeck scoring twice. Liverpool vs Brighton – Match preview and team news Date: Sunday, 25 October 2026 Kick-off: 14:00 BST Venue: Anfield Referee: Samuel Barrott Last meeting: Brighton 2-1 Liverpool, 21 March 2026, Premier League Team news Liverpool Dominik Szoboszlai is confirmed out with a hamstring injury, with Victor Munoz also sidelined. Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike and Jeremie Frimpong remain long-term absentees, though Bradley Barcola has received a positive fitness update and is in contention to start. Brighton Evan Ferguson, Stefanos Tzimas, Kaoru Mitoma, Femi Azeez and Zadok Yohanna are all unavailable through injury. Jason Steele, Pascal Struijk and Mats Wieffer are doubts, while Yankuba Minteh could feature from the bench on his first appearance of the season. Form Liverpool Liverpool have won three, drawn three and lost one of their seven Premier League matches, scoring nine goals and conceding eight. They have won four of their last five matches across all competitions, with their sole defeat coming against Manchester City. Brighton Brighton have won five, drawn one and lost one of their seven league matches, with 23 goals scored and only five conceded, the best goal difference outside the top two. They have won their last four matches in all competitions, most recently a 5-0 victory over Crystal Palace. Predicted lineups Liverpool possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Nyoni, Mac Allister; Barcola, Wirtz, Ngumoha; Isak Brighton possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen; Kadioglu, Dunk, Vuskovic, Boscagli; Gross, Andres; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas How to watch Liverpool vs Brighton & Hove Albion? The match will be broadcast live in the United Kingdom on Sky Sports. item.title: OTD (25/10/1966): George Herd’s Very Own ‘Match Of The Day’
item.description: The happy couple… George Herd was a fan favourite during his playing days at Roker Park and is still revered at Sunderland AFC nearly sixty years after making his final appearance for the Lads. A hugely energetic and infectious character, plus a popular face on the local non-scene in later years, when he passed away in 2024 there was an outpouring of emotion that proved just how much the community loved him —yet in 1966, it was a very different relationship that was being confirmed. Barbara Wright, a shorthand typist in a Sunderland office, had obviously taken a shine to George, for on Monday 24 October, the pair got married at St Luke’s Church in Pallion. Wanting to keep the ceremony secret, it wasn’t until the following day that most people got to find out about it, when the happy couple appeared in the local press and confirmed that following about six months of planning, everything had gone just as they’d hoped. After the ceremony, they’d gone to their new home in Cleadon before heading to a reception at Barbara’s parents’ house on Westmoor Road, rounding off the celebrations there. The newlyweds had first met at a dance around two years earlier but wanted a low-key event and the only other footballer at the service was George’s fellow Scot Bobby Kerr, who’d previously shared with him club digs on the appropriately-named Hampden Road behind the Fulwell End and Clock Stand. Exactly who it was that had invited him was not clear — maybe Kerr had been invited by the bride, keen to find out what living with her fiancé was going to be like! Whereas the nuptials and gone without a hitch however, the honeymoon period was much shorter than anticipated. Originally given leave of absence until Thursday by manager Ian McColl, Herd was disappointed to learn that his first full day of married life would instead see him having to report back to work, with the previous Saturday’s scheduled fixture against Stoke City having been rearranged at short notice and set to take on Tuesday evening. Initially called off due to a number of international games taking place that weekend, it was the Football League that insisted on the game taking place at the earliest opportunity, and that meant an early end to whatever the Herds had in mind. If there was to be any consolation for George, it was that he at least got to be part of victorious team, pulling off an impressive result against league leaders Stoke City, and that he had a direct hand in the winning goal. Now enjoying service of a different kind, his gift to his teammates was a perfectly-placed corner that was flicked on by George Mulhall and converted by Neil Martin in a 2-1 success. Herd was subsequently given a mark of seven out of ten in The Journal’s match report, and there are more details on the match available here.

item.title: Manchester United vs Bournemouth – Match preview and team news
item.description: Manchester United vs Bournemouth – Match preview and team news Manchester United host Bournemouth in a Premier League Gameweek 8 fixture at Old Trafford on Sunday, 25 October 2026. Michael Carrick’s United are 13th in the table with seven points from seven matches, one point and two places above Marco Rose’s Bournemouth. United go into the weekend off the back of a 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League, while Bournemouth beat AC Milan 3-0 in the Europa League in midweek and remain unbeaten in their last six meetings with United, winning none but drawing four and losing two of those encounters. The two sides drew 2-2 when they last met in March. Manchester United vs Bournemouth – Match preview and team news Date: Sunday, 25 October 2026 Kick-off: 14:00 BST Venue: Old Trafford Referee: Jarred Gillett Last meeting: Bournemouth 2-2 Manchester United, March 2026, Premier League Team news Manchester United Manuel Ugarte, Luke Shaw, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Kobbie Mainoo are all unavailable through injury. Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford and Lisandro Martinez missed the Como defeat but could return, and Leny Yoro is available again after a European suspension. Matheus Cunha and Noussair Mazraoui, both substituted at half-time in midweek, are unlikely to retain their places. Bournemouth Alex Toth, Julian Araujo and Alex Scott are all out through injury, while Junior Kroupi is a doubt with a foot problem. Djordje Petrovic returns in goal having been rested for the win over AC Milan, with Adam Smith expected to continue at right-back. Form Manchester United Manchester United have won one, drawn four and lost two of their seven Premier League matches, scoring 10 goals and conceding 10. They are winless in seven matches across all competitions following the midweek defeat to Como. Bournemouth Bournemouth have won one, drawn three and lost three of their seven league matches, with nine goals scored and 13 conceded. They have won their last two matches across all competitions, both with clean sheets, including a 3-0 win over AC Milan that kept their Europa League record unbeaten. Predicted lineups Manchester United possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, De Ligt, Dalot; Tielemans, Baleba; Amad, Fernandes, Rashford; Mbeumo Bournemouth possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Christie; Rayan, Cook, Tavernier; Evanilson How to watch Manchester United vs Bournemouth? The match will be broadcast live in the United Kingdom on Sky Sports. item.title: Leeds United XI vs Sunderland – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Leeds United XI vs Sunderland – Predicted lineup and team news Leeds United travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon looking to return to winning ways after being held at home by Manchester United. Daniel Farke’s side are seventh in the Premier League with 10 points from seven matches, six points clear of Sunday’s hosts. Leeds have lost just once in their opening seven fixtures and remain in contention for a top-five finish this season. Farke guided Leeds to the Championship title with 100 points last season, and his side’s composed start back in the Premier League contrasts with a Sunderland team already rooted to the bottom of the table. Leeds United team news Mateo Joseph (knee) and Joe Rodon (hamstring) are both out through injury. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a doubt with a bruised foot, while Noah Okafor and Anton Stach are both managing adductor issues. Dan James is also a doubt with a back problem. Calvert-Lewin has scored four goals this season and would be a notable miss if he fails to recover in time, while Stach’s 10 created chances have been a key creative outlet behind the front line when he has played. With Calvert-Lewin’s availability in question, Lukas Nmecha is set to lead the line, supported by Harry Wilson and Brenden Aaronson in behind. Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka are expected to continue anchoring midfield, with Jayden Bogle and Gabriel Gudmundsson providing width and defensive cover as wing-backs in Farke’s three-at-the-back system. James Justin, Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic are set to continue as the back three protecting goalkeeper James Trafford. No further fitness concerns have been reported elsewhere in Farke’s squad. Leeds United predicted lineup Leeds United possible starting XI (3-4-2-1): Trafford; Muharemovic, Elvedi, Justin; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha When will the match kick off? The Premier League match kicks off at 16:30 BST on Sunday, 25 October 2026. How to watch Sunderland vs Leeds United? The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK. item.title: Score Predictions - Leeds in the league - can we get a welcome win?
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 10: General view outside the stadium before the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Brighton & Hove Albion at Stadium of Light on October 10, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) Stats at a glance: Leeds (H) Premier League: 25/10/2026 Average home goals predicted: 1.25 Average away goals predicted: 0.62 Confidence of Roker Report’s writers: 5/10 Predicting a win for the Lads: 50% Martin Wanless (Cautious Optimist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 1 While a point away in Europe isn’t a bad result, and the performance was a bit better, it wasn’t the type of display that gives you huge confidence that all wrongs have been righted. Our finishing was appalling and we conceded some easy chances too, so we need to hope we make a further step in the right direction today. Leeds are a good side, and it’ll be a tough task to get a result but hopefully we’ll get something. Key differentiator: Robin Roefs — he can keep us in the game Confidence: 3/10 Bold call: Eight yellow cards to be dished out Malc Dugdale (Scarred happy clapper) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 0 If we can defend better, we showed in the week that we can create a lot. It’s just a case of continuing the progress with both aspects, scoring more than we miss, and we can get back to being ourselves. This will be a tight game for me and while it’s far from a ‘must win’ when we’re still less than ten games into the season, we can’t let the rot set in as this will both impact morale and put Régis Le Bris at risk — he deserves way more time than nine or ten games this season. Hopefully we have Brian Brobbey back and they don’t have Dominic Calvert-Lewin, though both players are subject to speculation about fitness. Let’s get the Stadium of Light back to being a home fortress with a clean sheet and a win, and shut down all these doom-mongers for a short while at least. Key differentiator: Brobbey up front and a resurgent Robin Roefs at the back, and we can take on anyone. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: One set piece goal will decide this either way, but hopefully in our favour. Jack Howe-Gingell (Eternal optimist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 2 Leeds 1 It’s one of those people are shouting about being a “must win” but a draw against an in-form Leeds team would be a great result (provided we can go to Coventry and win!). That said, I still fancy us to steal this one. I’m expecting an intense game and I think our fans will be edgy. We showed signs of life against Poznań, but we were too wasteful and it cost us the three points. Leeds will be a much better standard of opponent, and I have to hope we’ll be up to the task. Key differentiator: It’ll feel like a low-key derby on Sunday in my opinion, and despite reservations I think the players will go hard and amp the crowd up. Hopefully we have Brian Brobbey back and they don’t have Dominic Calvert-Lewin, though both players are subject to speculation about fitness. Let’s get the Stadium of Light back to being a home fortress with a clean sheet and a win, and shut down all these doom-mongers for a short while at least. Key differentiator: Brobbey up front and a resurgent Robin Roefs at the back, and we can take on anyone. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: One set piece goal will decide this either way, but hopefully in our favour. Jack Howe-Gingell (Eternal optimist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 2 Leeds 1 It’s one of those people are shouting about being a “must win” but a draw against an in-form Leeds team would be a great result (provided we can go to Coventry and win!). That said, I still fancy us to steal this one. I’m expecting an intense game and I think our fans will be edgy. We showed signs of life against Poznań, but we were too wasteful and it cost us the three points. Leeds will be a much better standard of opponent, and I have to hope we’ll be up to the task. Key differentiator: It’ll feel like a low-key derby on Sunday in my opinion, and despite reservations I think the players will go hard and amp the crowd up. Confidence: 6/10 Bold call: Both of our goals will be from set pieces. “Champion” Will Jones (Heart over head) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 1 A decent point in Poznań on Thursday, and hopefully something we can build on going into Sunday. We’ve had a mixed few weeks, but there were signs of a bit more fight in Europe, and now we need to bring that back to the Stadium of Light. Leeds will make it a proper battle, and I can see this being a tight one with neither side giving much away. The home crowd should give us a lift, but after the European trip, I reckon we might have to settle for a point. Key differentiator: Whoever wins the midfield battle and keeps their head in what could be a scrappy game. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: Our goal comes from a defender who hasn’t scored for Sunderland before. Matty Foster (Pragmatist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 0 Leeds 0 I honestly go into this not knowing what to predict. Leeds have a good start, only losing to Arsenal so far. Our league form isn’t great, but I’m trying not to fall into a negative state of mind. They’ve drawn most of their fixtures, and to go entirely “middle of the road”, I’m predicting more of the same again. Key differentiator: Whether Brian Brobbey is playing or not. I don’t envisage us scoring without him. Confidence: 4/10 Bold call: The woodwork will be hit on three or more occasions. Anthony Gair (Depreciating optimist) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 2 Leeds 0 In a game which is a very early “must win” for the mighty wizards, I think we’ll finally start hitting the target against a depleted — and hopefully toothless without Dominic Calvert-Lewin — Leeds side. I think we’ll come out all guns blazing, with the lads absolutely riled up and prepared to die for the shirt. It may lead to a lack of discipline at the back, but I think we’ll have enough to beat this incredibly impressive, Leeds team. Key differentiator: The crowd need to stay patient, support the lads and not get on their backs if they make an error. Confidence: 7/1 0 Bold call: There’ll be a red card in this one. Gary Winter (Glass almost empty) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 1 Leeds 1 It’s probably too soon to be calling out “must win” games this early in the season, as I do believe there’s plenty of time to turn the ship around — the sooner the better, though. Today feels really important, and a win would lift the mounting pressure and buy us just a little breathing space. Dread has already crept in more than it should, so a loss is hard to digest as, rightly or wrongly, panic will crank up several notches. Key differentiator: We could do with a really energetic performance, but after another away trip in Europe, I think the distance travelled will make that difficult. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: One or more goals scored between 15-30 minutes and one or more goals scored between 45-65 minutes. Brett Lyons-Davis (Gut feeling guy) says… Score prediction: Sunderland 2 Leeds 1 We go again — we need a win, simple as that. The lads did put on a much better performance in Poland and it was refreshing to see some shots and we could/should’ve scored more. Defensively, we did look vulnerable and had Robin Roefs not been on his game, we would be talking about another defeat. Key differentiator: Brian Brobbey. Confidence: 5/10 Bold call: Despite the game being between two tough Northern teams, there will be at least one goal scored by a player wearing gloves. Last game thoughts… Most will agree we should’ve beaten Lech Poznan in the week, but when we opened the game with our lone striker being Timor Tutierov due to wider injuries, scoring goals was always going to be a challenge. I was chuffed at him getting off the mark, but that should’ve been his second, as he made clear in his post-match interviews. Robin Roefs had a blinder and saved our blushes by helping us to an away draw, which many maybe would’ve taken before a ball was kicked since we already have two wins in the competition. A few players also put themselves in the first team shop window again, especially the likes of Jules Ahoka. Today’s challenge will be much sterner and we’ll have to bring all the best bits of our Europa campaign and minimal evidence of our errors and self-destructive moments to get a win against the White Rose. Who’s fit and who isn’t will be vital, too. Last game predictions… Four of the lads correctly called the somewhat deflating draw, but ‘Bold Call’ points were lacking this time around. The form of Grafter Gair continues to impress, with last seasons basement dweller continuing gathering points and holding on to the leaders as we move towards the ten games in the Premier League point. Predictions table and standings Gary and Matty continue their battle for top spot, with Gair chasing them down and hoping for mistakes to challenge for the lead. The peloton between fourth and seventh will also be hoping the leading lads slip up to allow the gap to close. Jack is now eleven points off the top, and much like our mighty Mackems, he needs to st

item.title: Fan Focus: What Can Sunderland expect From Daniel Farke’s Leeds?
item.description: POZNAN, POLAND - 2026/10/22: Nordi Mukiele (L), Timur Tuterov (C) and Nilson Angulo (R) of Sunderland celebrate a goal during the UEFA Europa League match between Lech Poznan and AFC Sunderland at Enea Stadium Poznan. Final score: Lech Poznan 1:1 AFC Sunderland. (Photo by Mikolaj Barbanell/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) Leeds comfortably secured Premier League survival last season, finishing fourteenth after promotion and also reaching the FA Cup semi-finals. How would you assess that first season back and what were your expectations heading into this campaign? A really successful first season back. I would’ve taken seventeenth on goal difference so to have such a strong end to the season was really promising. I don’t think any Leeds fans relaxed until we were mathematically safe, but it was so refreshing to see a Leeds team in the Premier League that didn’t embarrass us week after week and had grit and determination. Leeds currently sit seventh with ten points from their opening seven matches. Have you been surprised by how well the season has started, and has it changed what supporters believe this team can achieve? I’m not completely surprised as I think we handily upgraded the core of our team over the summer. You’ll always have a good start if you’re settled and we smartly upgraded the core of what’s a really settled unit. I think it’s made supporters realise we shouldn’t get drawn into any relegation battle. And some supporters will now believe we can achieve Europe this season. However, I personally disagree, and even though we’re solid, I think limitations mean that mid-table is what our team can realistically achieve. Daniel Farke has now had several years to shape this Leeds side and establish the club back in the Premier League. How highly is he regarded by supporters at this stage, and how has his approach evolved since promotion? It’s a weird one with Farke. I think the ghost of Marcelo Bielsa has hovered over every appointment since, and Daniel has certainly struggled with matching the expectations created by Marcelo. However, Farke is regarded highly — even if grudgingly — by some supporters. He has massively evolved since promotion and is now far more pragmatic and manages to squeeze a lot more out of a unit than he ever seemed to before. Even when we were flying in the Championship, a lot of that seemed to be because of the players rather than him. However, despite how well he’s doing and has evolved, I think there still is a ceiling if he want to progress beyond just being solid. Saying that, though, he’s a very steady captain of the ship and you need to appreciate what you’ve got, because things could go downhill rapidly without him. Leeds drew 1-1 with Manchester United last weekend, having also beaten Newcastle 4-1 and taken a point away at Brighton already this season. Which performance has given you the most encouragement so far? That point away at Brighton is looking better by the week! But I think the Newcastle
item.content:encoded: POZNAN, POLAND - 2026/10/22: Nordi Mukiele (L), Timur Tuterov (C) and Nilson Angulo (R) of Sunderland celebrate a goal during the UEFA Europa League match between Lech Poznan and AFC Sunderland at Enea Stadium Poznan. Final score: Lech Poznan 1:1 AFC Sunderland. (Photo by Mikolaj Barbanell/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) Leeds comfortably secured Premier League survival last season, finishing fourteenth after promotion and also reaching the FA Cup semi-finals. How would you assess that first season back and what were your expectations heading into this campaign? A really successful first season back. I would’ve taken seventeenth on goal difference so to have such a strong end to the season was really promising. I don’t think any Leeds fans relaxed until we were mathematically safe, but it was so refreshing to see a Leeds team in the Premier League that didn’t embarrass us week after week and had grit and determination. Leeds currently sit seventh with ten points from their opening seven matches. Have you been surprised by how well the season has started, and has it changed what supporters believe this team can achieve? I’m not completely surprised as I think we handily upgraded the core of our team over the summer. You’ll always have a good start if you’re settled and we smartly upgraded the core of what’s a really settled unit. I think it’s made supporters realise we shouldn’t get drawn into any relegation battle. And some supporters will now believe we can achieve Europe this season. However, I personally disagree, and even though we’re solid, I think limitations mean that mid-table is what our team can realistically achieve. Daniel Farke has now had several years to shape this Leeds side and establish the club back in the Premier League. How highly is he regarded by supporters at this stage, and how has his approach evolved since promotion? It’s a weird one with Farke. I think the ghost of Marcelo Bielsa has hovered over every appointment since, and Daniel has certainly struggled with matching the expectations created by Marcelo. However, Farke is regarded highly — even if grudgingly — by some supporters. He has massively evolved since promotion and is now far more pragmatic and manages to squeeze a lot more out of a unit than he ever seemed to before. Even when we were flying in the Championship, a lot of that seemed to be because of the players rather than him. However, despite how well he’s doing and has evolved, I think there still is a ceiling if he want to progress beyond just being solid. Saying that, though, he’s a very steady captain of the ship and you need to appreciate what you’ve got, because things could go downhill rapidly without him. Leeds drew 1-1 with Manchester United last weekend, having also beaten Newcastle 4-1 and taken a point away at Brighton already this season. Which performance has given you the most encouragement so far? That point away at Brighton is looking better by the week! But I think the Newcastle one is still the most encouraging. Our biggest weakness is probably our attacking unit (Dominic Calvert-Lewin aside) and so any performance where we score goals is encouraging. The Manchester United result is weirdly pretty disappointing as right now, our biggest rivals feel there for the taking. The club made seven additions during the summer, including James Trafford, Harry Wilson, Tarik Muharemović and Nico Elvedi. How happy were you with the transfer window and which of the new signings has impressed you most? We’ve had our fair share of bad transfer windows so Leeds fans are often wary and usually assume we’re going to “mess things up” (deadline day has been particularly painful). However, on reflection, it was a great transfer window and really created a solid unit that will always make you competitive. Muharemović was an inspired signing and Nico Elvedi also looks like a great one. Harry Wilson the only one that has been pretty disappointing so far and doesn’t look quite up to our intensity. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is Leeds’ leading scorer with four Premier League goals and has earned an England recall, although he’s a doubt for today through injury. How important has he become to this team? I can’t sing DCL’s praises enough. He’s the perfect striker in his all-round play and we look far better when he plays. People talk about his finishing but when he does everything right, and still scores, you can’t really complain. If he doesn’t play vs Sunderland, we’ll be far worse off for it. Calvert-Lewin, Anton Stach and Noah Okafor are all major doubts for the trip to Sunderland, while Joe Rodon remains out, although Daniel James is back in contention. How much would those potential absences affect Leeds today? Massively. DCL is so important for us. Stach is an absolute monster in the middle and Okafor is our main spark in attack. If all three are out, that’s 100% advantage Sunderland but Farke has often exaggerated things and plays mind games with these things. Leeds have recently been using a 3-4-2-1 system, with Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka playing important roles through the middle. What are the biggest strengths of this side tactically, and where are they still vulnerable? Biggest strengths: central midfield, centre backs, wing backs. A very solid unit that always looks competitive even when not playing that well. Our set pieces and physicality are also very suited for the Premier League. Weaknesses: DCL and Okafor are great, but in attack it often can look like we don’t have much of a plan except to launch it up to DCL, and can look flat. If you also allow us to dominate and sit on the counter we lack creativity, we can look far stronger on the counter. I still think Farke is limited in tactical nous compared to the best managers in this league and this lack of tactical flexibility can be exposed. Sunderland took four points from Leeds last season, drawing 1-1 at the Stadium of Light before winning 1-0 at Elland Road. From what you’ve seen of Sunderland since, where do you think they can cause Leeds the most problems on Sunday? From sitting back and hitting us on the counter. Régis Le Bris has looked tactically superior in a few of the games and if we don’t get an early goal or Sunderland do, it could be a tough watch with us trying to break Sunderland down. Finally, what type of game are you expecting at the Stadium of Light? Who do you think could be the difference-maker for Leeds and what is your score prediction? I expect a very cagey game. Sunderland need the win and we will be pretty tight as always in defence. I’d love to see Wilson finally pay back his big wages and show how he can be a difference maker in attack, especially with some of our big attackers injured. I’ve put 1-0 to Sunderland on my Super 6, but I’ve got to back my team if I’m representing us here, so I’m going to go 0-1 Leeds, with the winner being a Wilson free kick.

item.title: Newcastle United XI vs Crystal Palace – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Newcastle United XI vs Crystal Palace – Predicted lineup and team news Newcastle United travel to Selhurst Park on Sunday afternoon looking to halt a run of three defeats in their last four Premier League matches. Matthias Jaissle’s side are 11th in the table with eight points from seven games, having won three of their opening five matches in charge before a recent downturn that includes a 4-1 defeat to Coventry City and a 1-0 loss to Aston Villa. Newcastle have scored just four goals across their last four matches, a marked drop-off from the attacking form that marked the early weeks of Jaissle’s reign. Newcastle sit third-bottom of the Premier League’s form table over the last five matches, underlining the scale of the task facing Jaissle this weekend. Newcastle United team news Jacob Ramsey is unlikely to feature because of a thigh injury, with Jaissle keen not to rush the midfielder back into the squad. Tino Livramento (knee) and Ewen Jaouen (thigh) are also out. Matias Fernandez-Pardo is a doubt with illness and Anthony Elanga with a thigh issue, and both will be assessed closer to kick-off. Harvey Barnes leads the squad for assists and big chances created this season, while only Elanga and Joe Willock have scored more than once. If Elanga is passed fit, he is expected to continue on the left of an attacking trio, but Jacob Murphy and William Osula look the more likely options to support Wissa if he is unavailable. Nico Gonzalez and Joelinton are set to continue as the central midfield pairing, with Lewis Miley, Malick Thiaw, Sven Botman and Lewis Hall forming the back four protecting goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek. Newcastle United predicted lineup Newcastle United possible starting XI (4-2-3-1): Hornicek; Miley, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Gonzalez, Joelinton; Murphy, Osula, Barnes; Wissa When will the match kick off? The Premier League match kicks off at 14:00 BST on Sunday, 25 October 2026. How to watch Crystal Palace vs Newcastle United? The match will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK. item.title: Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems go | Barney Ronay
item.description: Home side broke the game open with some unique corner routines, but a goalkeeping error ruined the plan There was an odd interlude at Stamford Bridge with 76 minutes gone and the score still 0-0, one of those moments where suddenly your brain seems to be on inside out, like trying to walk the wrong way down an escalator. Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. item.dc:creator: Barney Ronay at Stamford Bridge
item.content:encoded: Home side broke the game open with some unique corner routines, but a goalkeeping error ruined the plan There was an odd interlude at Stamford Bridge with 76 minutes gone and the score still 0-0, one of those moments where suddenly your brain seems to be on inside out, like trying to walk the wrong way down an escalator. Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. Continue reading...

item.title: Why Stanley Matthews’ Ballon d’Or triumph echoes down the years for Harry Kane | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In 1956, the Blackpool great was recognised for his force of individual will, the very thing that makes the Bayern and England striker the standout candiate Systems football began In 1963 (On the hallowed turf at Wembley) With the impact of a cynical foul By Gino Pivatelli. At that moment in the European Cup final, when the hard-working Milan forward, brought in to combat Benfica’s Mário Coluna, caught the great playmaker, football of the individual came to an end. The foul not only checked a promising break, but broke a bone in Coluna’s foot. Without substitutes, he hobbled on, diminished, and Milan won 2-1 to lift the trophy and register the first victory for a team that prioritised the system over the individual. Modern football was born. Continue reading...

item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
item.description: Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone; Dundee United 3-2 Aberdeen Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday , the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy. Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining. This story will be updated after Sunday’s matches Continue reading...

item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
item.description: Head coach in hospital after collapsing in training Assistant coach Aaron Danks to take charge against Freiburg Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition. Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined. Continue reading...

item.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
item.description: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, José Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico. Not yet anyway, but it’s time: on Sunday night he returns to the stadium he first arrived at 30 transformative years ago as Bobby Robson’s talented young translator, and last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football. The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too. Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
item.description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the clouds If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern‑day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win against Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
